utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Maybe before the witness comes to the courtroom, the next witness is Mr. Abdylhaqim Shaqiri, I wanted to make an application to add certain items to our exhibit list if this is possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's possible for you to make application.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yeah. And I'm referring here to two items, first pictures, 18 pictures which have been provided by this witness on occasion of his last testimony. During the proofing session the witness came and brought certain items. This was in 2006. And the second item I'm referring to is videotape which was also brought to the Office of the Prosecutor on occasion of the last proofing, and I'm referring again to the proofing in 2006. What has happened was that the material had been provided late, meaning shortly before the witness's testimony, to the Office of the Prosecutor. The videotape is two hours long, and there was no chance to review the video before the witness testified in the Milutinovic case. The Defence in the Milutinovic case had been also informed about that fact, that there were reasons of time constraints. The Office of the Prosecutor disclosed both items in -- on the 11th of December, 2007, to the Defence in the Djordjevic case. So our application is it had been in the possession for more than one year and five months, and we have also informed on Monday this week when this witness came and told us again about the videotape the Defence of Mr. Djordjevic about the fact that we are intending to use this videotape and a few pictures. Yeah, this will be my application, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Your explanation for it not having been on the list or each of these items?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I can say that the videotape was reviewed only following Monday since the witness told us that there is certain items on the videotape. And we informed the Defence before even having reviewed the tape about -- that we are seeking eventually to use it, and now having reviewed it in its entirety, we also prepared certain stills out of the video. We would like to use that video, Your Honours. We also made another copy for the Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The point I'm asking is your explanation for not having put this on your list before the commencement of this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Before the commencement of this trial, I can only say it has not been reviewed until then. It was, so to speak, some kind of a mission which I'm trying to rectify. And we believe that we have at least given appropriate notice to the Defence. As I stated, the Defence is in no way surprised about this item which has been disclosed in December 2007 already, Your Honours. We don't see any unfairness. We admit that we could have put it on our list earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The other material issue for us is what is the significance of these items? How material is it in the case?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I can explain that, Your Honours. The video is -- and your -- the witness will explain that if I'm eventually allowed to use it. The video was taken after the return of the witness from Macedonia back to his village, and it shows destruction of houses as well as destruction of the mosque. This witness is an imam and, yeah, there's a sequence of about a minute duration which we have identified showing exactly - and it's a 360-degree view of the destruction of the mosque - how it was when the witness returned. So it goes to destruction of cultural property on the one side, as well as damage and destruction of buildings which is charged as part of Count 5 in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The video, then, is merely supporting the oral evidence that the witness will give?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. There was an issue that this witness is the only witness coming from that particular village, Prilepnica, in the Milutinovic trial, and we don't have any other witness coming here during this trial to corroborate, so to speak, the witness's oral account. And in the Prosecution's view, this video could be taken as at least partially confirming the witness's account.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, what about the photographs?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The photographs relate to the same issue of destruction, and we have selected -- there are two photographs relating again to the mosque.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I strenuously object to the admission of this evidence, to the adding of this evidence to the list of the Prosecution for two reasons. You have already clarified the first reason. Namely, before Monday or whatever day this week the OTP did not even hint at this possibility. I would like to say that in the notification of the 28th of August, it is stated that the witness had brought certain video footage, but I would like to say immediately that it is in issue what exactly this footage is. A Danish film is mentioned but also home video taken by some villager, and the witness was not an eye-witness to the damaging of the mosque. We have here an expert coming to testify to the circumstances of damage inflicted to religious buildings, and the photographs had been -- have been known to the Prosecution for a long time. The witness brought them in 2006, and these photographs were not taken by the witness but by a third person. That is why I object to the admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you mean to say at line 6 the 28th of August or the 28th of April, that notification was given?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was talking about the 28th of August, 2006, when the Defence team in Milutinovic was notified, and we got an overview of supplemental information in April, on the 28th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber is of the view, Mr. Neuner, that it would be not a proper exercise of its discretion to allow this additional evidence, in view of the long neglect of it in the preparation of the Prosecution case. So we uphold Mr. Djurdjic's submission. If the witness is ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Would you please read aloud the affirmation which is now shown to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down. Mr. Neuner has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What is your name and date of birth?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Abdylhaqim Shaqiri. I was born on the 6th of March, 1949.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Shaqiri, what is your occupation, and where do you live?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: I am imam, and I live in Prilepnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is it correct that in September 2006 you testified in the Milutinovic et al. case?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you had an opportunity before coming here today to review your transcript?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And does this transcript of testimony truly and accurately reflect what you would say if you gave your evidence orally today in court?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm referring to 65 ter number 5073 and would seek to tender this into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00729, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm reading out a summary of this witness's evidence. The witness, an Albanian male, is an imam in the village of Prilepnica in the municipality of Gnjilane. On 6th of April, 1999, he heard gun-fire in Prilepnica and saw soldiers with two civilians held at gunpoint. The soldiers claimed to look for KLA members and ordered him to make an announcement over the loud-speakers of the mosque that all villagers should leave the village until noon the next day. The witness complied. The witness saw soldiers seizing money, property, identification documents, and vehicles. About 3.000 people left Prilepnica in the direction of Gnjilane. En route they had to pass through several check-points manned by Serb military and police. They were followed by police from one such check-point, who told them they had to return and nothing would happen to them. When they returned to Prilepnica the following day, one house was burned and many damaged. On 13 of April, 1999, the villagers of Prilepnica were again ordered by soldiers to leave. The following morning the village was surrounded by tanks, armoured vehicles, and five times as many soldiers as on 6 April 1999. 3.000 villagers gathered in their cars and tractors and were escorted out of the village. The size of the convoy increased as it was joined by people from other villages. Some of the villages they passed through were empty and houses were burning. Again, they had to pass through check-points where they were abused and at one stage had to pay money to be able to pass safely to Tetovo and Macedonia. End of the summary. Your Honours, I would seek to tender the documents associated with the transcript I have just tendered because they were all discussed at length in the Milutinovic case. Could I seek to tender 65 ter number 5074?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, what is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: That is an in-court exhibit used in the Milutinovic case and annotated by the witness, a map with some markings, and it's all explained in the transcript, Your Honours, as I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It just helps us to recall which of these particular documents you're referring to, if you can give --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I will do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- a quick verbal description rather than merely the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I will do so, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00730, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The next proposed exhibit is 5075, it's again an in-court exhibit in the Milutinovic case, again a map marked by the witness Shaqiri in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00731, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: 5076 is the next exhibit. It's again an in-court exhibit, a map annotated by this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It, too, will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00732, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And I have then map 5077, again and an in-court exhibit marked by this witness former P24 in the Milutinovic case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00733, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And this being said, the Prosecution has to further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Neuner. Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have few questions for Mr. Shaqiri.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Shaqiri.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Veljko Djurdjic, I'm a member of the Defence team. I'm Veljko Djurdjic, member of the Defence team for the accused, Vlastimir Djordjevic. I'm assisted by Ms. Marie O'Leary, member of our team as well, and I'd only like to hear from you a few clarifications. In 1999 who were the members of your household?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: In 1999, if you're referring to the 6th of April, I lived with my mother, my brothers, myself, and I had some refugees staying in our house, refugees from Drenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the tradition of the Muslim Albanian population in the country-side, is it customary for a house to be surrounded by a wall?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did your own family estate have a wall around it?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: My house, my private house in the village doesn't have a wall; one part has, another doesn't. But where I was staying, at my mother's place, the house was walled off.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement I read that you were a teacher of the Albanian language for 23 years; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: [B/C/S interpretation] Yes, a teacher of Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you work in a school?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Yes, for 23 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And if I added up the years correctly, you became imam in 1996?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Shaqiri, when did you first hear of the existence of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: [Albanian interpretation] I think it was on the 28th of November, 1998, if I'm not mistaken at the funeral ceremony of a teacher. That's when for the first time the KLA publicly appeared in Drenica. I learned about this through the media, through television.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that you have no real knowledge about the KLA?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd also like to know, how do you know that there were no members of the KLA in your village in March 1999?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Not only in my village, but in the whole area known as Ana e Moraves, I never came across a KLA member, and I never heard from anyone that there was a KLA presence there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But the fact that you never heard of them and do not know of any does not mean necessarily that there weren't any; right?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: I am imam, person who visited different villages on a religious duty, and nobody ever said to me that there was a KLA presence in our area, in Ana e Moraves, except for in Drenica. This part here, where we were, was free of KLA presence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have just three more questions for you. They relate to the transcript of your testimony in the Milosevic trial. I'll give a reference and tell you what it's about. The first question concerns page 2779, lines 4 through 11, of the transcript in Milosevic, now it's Exhibit - just a moment - P729 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you mean the Milutinovic trial? You said Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Milutinovic I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This passage concerns your conversation with the officer nicknamed Rus. You said: "I heard the other officers call him 'Russian.' He wasn't Russian by ethnicity; it was just his nickname. I asked him not to make us leave the village because the population was mostly unemployed, and they were bound to their own houses. I told him we had never had any problems in the past, and here is what he told me: 'I see that you are an honourable man. The order has come from Belgrade. People have to be transferred from Prilepnica.'" Mr. Shaqiri, until the Milutinovic trial you never mentioned in any of the statements this part, that the orders had come from Belgrade that people be transferred from Prilepnica.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: I was asked to explain in detail the conversation I had with the Serb army officer nicknamed Rus or Russian, and I did explain in detail this conversation and what you just read out depicts exactly what he told me. Some things are very hard to be forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Shaqiri, in the statement you gave on the 25th of April, 1999, regarding this exchange, in paragraph 22 you say: "The commander asked me if I was an imam. I said yes." In paragraph 23, in English it's page 3, paragraph 3 from the top, you said: "He said, Look what's going on here. We received information that this village would be bombed by NATO, and we'll prevent it by all possible means. I am a commander and it is my duty" -- I apologise to the interpreters. "I am commander, and it is my duty to lay mines on all the roads in this village as well as all the surrounding hills. Therefore, you must leave the village within two hours because it is dangerous here." Mr. Shaqiri, that's your statement of the 25th of April, and this part about orders coming from Belgrade to transfer people from Prilepnica is nowhere to be found. This exchange, by the way, relates to the 6th of April.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. We're talking about two officers. You think that there is only one. The Russian is one officer and what you just read is a conversation that I had with the second officer. So we are talking about two different persons here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Shaqiri, you have to believe me if I say that this Russian is not mentioned anywhere in the statement of the 25th of April, but it doesn't matter which officer it is, the first, second, or third. This statement about orders coming from Belgrade is nowhere to be found. That's the point I'm trying to make.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: It is possible that I didn't mention -- when I did give my statement, I quoted the conversation I had with the officers in that group, and the Russian is another officer with whom I spoke in private. And that's why it is possible that I failed to mention him, or maybe I wasn't asked about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to show you another -- read to you another passage from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, you are referring to a statement of the witness which we don't have. We have the transcript but not the statement. Now, is this a document that is in e-court?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I apologise. This will be the Defence document D -- just a moment. Let me look it up. I apologise. D003-0001. This is a statement of 25th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, and it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, because I can't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Shaqiri, will you believe me when I say that you did not mention this, either in your 2001 statement or in your 2002 statement?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Now I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have on the screens D003-0016.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Shaqiri, in this statement which is somewhat briefer, shorter, you never mentioned -- never mention any conversation with an officer and this reference of the order having been sent from Belgrade. Can you see that statement before you?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I would like to ask the court officer whether he's heard the number for the second statement. The second statement is D003-0016. Oh, I see, so it's on the screen already.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Shaqiri, do you agree with me --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I just interrupt at this point because the Prosecution believes this is not a proper course of action to show this witness the cover sheet of his statement and then, yeah, ask him simply whether he didn't remember stating about conversation with an officer. We believe the appropriate course of action would be to walk the witness to the particular passage of his statement where he has addressed that day or that particular moment and then show that there is eventually an omission. But just to show the cover page after the witness has stated on the record that he can't remember, we believe is inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Neuner. I think it would be more help to the witness and to the Chamber, Mr. Djurdjic, if you were to direct the witness's attention to the part in which he discusses the events but does -- where you say there's no mention of the conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, but in this second statement of 2001, because this is a sort of a supplemental statement, there is no mention of those matters, and there is also no mention of what I mentioned in the beginning, that this order had come from Belgrade. Could we please now see pages 2 of both the Albanian and English versions?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Here, if you look at the fifth and sixth paragraph, you will see that nothing is mentioned there. Mr. Shaqiri, have you read the statement?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Yes, I looked at some parts of it, the ones that are on the screen. But if I may, I'd like to reply with one sentence. All those who have taken statements from me have come to ask me some questions, telling me that they had other information. If I wanted to provide further information they said to me that they already had that. So I think that this is not a complete recount of what happened from the beginning to the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Shaqiri, this type of information is so significant that no investigator of this Tribunal would fail to mention such statement, but all right. This is your explanation, and there is no reason for me to further -- put further questions about this. Now I would like to talk about the 13th of April and refer you again to your statement of the 25th of April, or rather, since we already have this before us, let's stay with this same document. Mr. Shaqiri, on page 2800, lines 3 to 6 of the Milosevic [as interpreted] transcript, I will read out your answer to a question put. "A. One could see that they have an expression of satisfaction on their faces, and they said, It's good that we found you. We apologise, but the order has come from the supreme staff in Belgrade that Prilepnica had to be evacuated." And you I would like to go back to your 1999 statement, the one of 25th April, D003-0001 --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I just for the record state that this is again the Milutinovic transcript from which this quote came. I believe my learned colleague has inadvertently mentioned again Milosevic transcript. It is the Milutinovic transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You're absolutely right, my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now I will read out paragraph 47, that's on page 4 in the English version, paragraph 1; and in the Albanian version that is on page 4, paragraph 3. "On the 13th of April, 1999, on a Tuesday around 11.30 some soldiers came" --

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Just a second. The transcript is in Serbian, not in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please display the Albanian translation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [B/C/S interpretation] Well, if you don't have it in Albanian, it's okay, no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, I'll tell you, Mr. Shaqiri, I do have the Albanian version. Let me see -- in fact, let me check whether I actually do have it. No, apparently I don't have the Albanian version either of this 1999 statement. This was a statement of 25th of April, 1999. So, Mr. Shaqiri, the point that I'm trying to make is that then, too, you did not mention that this order had come from the supreme staff in Belgrade that Prilepnica had to be evacuated, and this is in reference to that conversation of 13 of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt at this point, but the witness has said he would like to look at an Albanian version. We have also checked our records. We don't have one here in the courtroom. Maybe the more appropriate course is to make a break at this point in time and provide the witness with an Albanian version, but he can't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is there an Albanian version available to you, Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, but I think that the witness can also read Serbian. Unfortunately, I only have the English and B/C/S versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Shaqiri, would it be difficult for you to read the Serbian?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: [Albanian interpretation] Yes, I understood the question, and I'm trying to help you out, you and the honourable Court. Because during the Milutinovic trial, I gave a very clear explanation. I mentioned the conversation with two officers Djilas and Palmarevic who didn't mention Belgrade. He simply said that we have orders from above. Djilas said, and I explained, that his driver who worked in the same factory, in the course of conversation he told the driver that the order had come from above, and we were there present and heard it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I take it from an answer you have already given, Mr. Shaqiri, that you are able to read the language version that's on the screen in front of you. I think you said it was no --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The letters are very small. If you can enlarge them, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that clear enough for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is -- in the transcript the conversation is that of the 6th, not the 13th, what I mentioned earlier when I went to the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have page 5 of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you see it now? That's page 5. Please take a look at the second portion where it says "on the 13th of April," and then read that portion and onwards. Can you see it now? Please just look at this where you said: "The order has come from the Supreme Command in Belgrade ..."

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: It's not here. I don't find it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you find that portion? "I knew these three soldiers, they were from Gnjilane. One of them was called ..." So read from there on. "Djilas spoke then. He said he had received orders from the regular Serbian army ..." So that portion.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: [B/C/S interpretation] Yes, I knew these three soldiers. [Albanian interpretation] It should have been said "officer," it's not right, the word chosen in Serbian. [B/C/S interpretation] One of them was called Luba as written, probably Ljuba, Palmarevic, yes, a lawyer, yes. He had a green uniform worn by the regular Serbian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Shaqiri, just please mind this. What I'm saying is that here you did not mention that the order had come from the Supreme Command in Belgrade that Prilepnica had to be evacuated. So that is not in this statement, that portion. That's all I'm asking you about. I'm not making -- I have no questions about the other portions; I'm just interested in this part.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: [Albanian interpretation] I don't know how the translation was done, but I said what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We also have the English version, and it's missing from the English version as well.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to show me the Albanian original because both versions are translations. Because there are two words there, from above that Ljuba mentioned and from Belgrade, but not to me, to his own driver. He told his driver, Reshat, that the order had come from above, from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know whether we should ask the Prosecution to provide this statement of 25th of April. I just wanted to ask this witness whether he could confirm that this is what he actually said, and then to tender these documents so that they can be compared with a transcript in the Milutinovic trial. I would appreciate it if you could provide further instructions to me regarding this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Have you put to the witness the passages from the statement of the 25th of April, 1999, that you suggest are different from what he now says?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and the other ones too. And the witness looked at the Serbian version of that statement, and he made a comment but he also commented that he did not have the Albanian version before him. Because this is not to do with the 6th of April. We're now talking about the paragraphs dealing with the 13th of April. That's on page 5 of the B/C/S version, as of 13th of April, and then on the next page through the end of the page. And nowhere in that portion is there any mention of these quotation -- the words that I quoted from the Milutinovic trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And you've put to the witness the passages concerning the earlier discussion from that statement? It became rather confused, Mr. Djurdjic, what you were doing. And I'm wanting to be sure that you have put to the witness all the passages that you suggest are relevant to this question concerning both discussions with army officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will try to be quite clear. In the 25th of April, 1999, statement with regards to the conversation that was held on the 13th of April, this conversation with army officers, these were in paragraphs on page 5 from the words "as of April 13th, 1999," and in the following paragraphs on the next page. So that's where the words of the witness that refer to the same event as the one where in the Milutinovic case the witness said an order had come from Belgrade that Prilepnica had to be evacuated. So what I'm saying is that both in this June 2001 and the 2002 statements by the witness, those words are missing or that statement is missing. Well, I think that I put to the witness in fairness the portion where it says that they discussed -- they talked to the officer on the 13th, and then they left Prilepnica, and we see this conversation with a man called Palmarevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, I'm just wanting to be sure that you have put the passages on which you rely because we will be focusing on those at a later time. And you've also mentioned the 2002 statement. Have you put that to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'll do it now. That is the statement of 2002 which is very short. And again, I don't have the Albanian version before me. I just have this in the English and B/C/S languages. This is D003-0040. [In English] Of 5th February 2002. [Interpretation] Could we now please see this statement of 5 February 2002, that's D003-0040, and 0044 is the Albanian version. So D003-0044 is the same statement in the Albanian version. Could we please see the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Shaqiri, am I correct in saying that your words are also omitted from this correction to your statement of 2002?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: I have made these corrections because I found technical mistakes in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I agree, but on this occasion, too, you failed to mention what I've read out to you when I quoted your words in the Milutinovic case. And I'm just asking you now whether it is true that those -- that part of the statement is also omitted from this correction of 2002?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You would now like, Mr. Djurdjic, to tender the statements? You start first with the statement of the 25th of April, 1999. That will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That statement, Your Honours, is under document ID D003-0001 would be assigned D00094.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And then the next statement of the 19th and 22nd of June, 2001; is that so, Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That statement, Your Honours, is under document ID D003-0016 would be assigned D00095.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Then the corrections in 2002?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is D003-0040.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here it is 4445 -- 0045 is the number I have here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the Albanian version of this document.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Just one more question, Mr. Shaqiri --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Djurdjic. We're waiting for it to come up so that it can be received. It's there now. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned D00096, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, for this assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Shaqiri, just one more question, or rather, I'd like to know this. Am I right in saying that you and your compatriots in 1998 and 1999 while you were in Prilepnica had no problems whatsoever with the Serbian police?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Can you ask the question again, please, I want to hear it again. [B/C/S interpretation] Could you tell me the question again because I hear a double voice in my ears.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that you and your fellow villagers in Prilepnica had no problems whatsoever with the Serbian police in 1998 and 1999 before you left the village?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: [Albanian interpretation] It is correct. We never had any problems with the police of Gjilan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Shaqiri.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have completed my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djurdjic. Mr. Neuner, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: A few questions, Your Honours. If I could have - and I've only the 65 ter number at this point, I know it was tendered - 5075 is the -- it's P731 I'm told. Could I have P731.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And I'm pulling this map up, Witness, because you were just asked about the police. Could you briefly tell me where in the area in and around Prilepnica was the police stationed, if at all, in the events of the first half of April 1999?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: There was no police station as such, but on the 6th of April when the police came, this police was not from Gjilan. It was different police. I didn't know these people. Police and army because their uniforms differed. The movement of the convoy on their orders from our village towards Korstul [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to take this one by one. Can you first of all tell Your Honours here on the map which you have annotated in the Milutinovic trial, where is your village Prilepnica? Just state a number for Your Honours' benefit, please.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Prilepnica is number 1. Kmetofc is number 2, this is a different village. There was army stationed there --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm asking you for the police so far.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Police, as far as police is concerned, only at Kmetofc village and the village marked with number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Kmetofc village is marked with which number, please?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You just mentioned that -- and I believe you referred to the 6th of April, the police was there in the place you encircled as number 2. How or where exactly did you see the police there, in what fashion? You mentioned that they were not having a police station earlier, but how did you see the police there?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: This was traffic police, a regular patrol. They were at Kmetofc village.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what were they doing when you saw them on the 6th of April, 1999?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: The police only looked at us, whereas the army was the one that stopped us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. And can you describe the relationship, if any, between the police and the army at the place you encircled as number 2?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: The police was separate from the army. Maybe there were about 20 to 50 metres apart between the police and the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And how many policemen did you observe on the 6th of April, 1999?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: There were two or three traffic policemen there, not a large group.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. Then can you confirm briefly that this map here running from number 1 to number 5 is, in fact, depicting the route your convoy took on the 6th of April?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you by just referring to the numbers indicate to Your Honours where you, if at all, saw the police again having passed the place you mentioned or encircled with number 2?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Number 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please wait for a minute, Mr. Shaqiri. Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think I gave any cause for the explanation of this map in my cross-examination, and if it is necessary, perhaps the witness could have drawn a new map in direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, the concern is how does this arise in re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yeah. I'm only dwelling on this map in relation to the police. I'm, as Your Honours could observe, trying to stop the witness when he talks about the army and so on. I'm asking these questions because my learned colleague has asked about the relationship between the witness or the villagers of Prilepnica and the police. And I'm merely focusing on the police component of that witness's evidence. I'm just trying to show a slightly different picture, Your Honour. I'm mindful of not dwelling into any new areas; I'm confining myself to the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please carry on, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you now just answer the question, Witness. Where on your way on the 6th of April did you see apart from number 2 the police again, if at all?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: At number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And which type of police did you observe at number 4, and where were they stationed?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Again, traffic police, but the number of policemen was bigger, five or six policemen there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And when your convoy was walking, what were the policemen doing?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: They asked about our whereabouts, where we were heading to, on whose orders. We told him that we had nothing to do with the police, that we received this order from the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And where, if at all, did you see the police other than at number 2 and number 4 on the 6th of April, 1999?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: No, but these policemen from number 4 came to number 5 and told us to go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. If I could have now - and this refers to a map from the 13th of April - the exhibit number P732 on the ELMO -- or, sorry, on the e-court. P732. Just in one sentence or two what were you marking here in the course of the Milutinovic case?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Again, the movement of the convoy from my village towards Macedonia, but from the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And that is on what day?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: 14th April 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you have marked here four numbers. At which of these numbers, if at any, did you or the convoy encounter the police?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Just before Gjilan we were escorted by a police patrol throughout the journey.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you --

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Up to Dugane.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: From what point onwards were you escorted by the police?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: At the junction about 2 kilometres away from the village. As we left the village when we arrived at this junction, one policeman escorted us up to Livoc, and from Livoc we were escorted by four policemen. On the way we came to two different check-points, and there we saw different people, not regular police --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I just stop you here for a second. First tell me -- you said 2 kilometres away from the village you were escorted by the police. Which village were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: My village, Prilepnica. So from Prilepnica up to the main road we walked on our own. And from there up to Livoc we were escorted by one policeman. From Livoc onwards we were escorted by four policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you find Livoc here on the map in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Yes. You see Gjilan here. Number 1 is Livoc, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can we maybe for the witness's benefit enlarge that so that he can see that this is Livoc.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just before number 1 is Livoc. Now it's better. So up to Livoc we were escorted by one policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can we now have the entire map, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, Witness, where, if at any other point, did you encounter or the convoy encounter the police?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: As far as other policemen or people dressed in uniforms, different uniforms, are concerned, we saw them at number 2 at Partesh and at Kllokot.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Starting with number 2, how many policemen did you observe there?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: There, there were people with different uniforms. There were policemen mixed with other people wearing different uniforms. We were threatened there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry --

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: We had to pass through a barbed wire.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You're not answering my question. I'm asking you how many policemen were you observing at this place encircled with a number 2.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: According to the uniforms they wore, they were not regular policemen. They were not policemen from the town. They were different.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm just asking you for a number, not for the uniforms as such. How many persons you would qualify as being in the police you --

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: More than 20 I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And then you mentioned other places where you saw them. Partesh, how many policemen did you observe at Partesh?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: At Partesh all of them were military, mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And at Kllokot, did you observe any police at Kllokot?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: What we spoke earlier refers to Kllokot.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is that place mentioned with a number here on the map in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Kllokot is at number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. Then I have just a few questions --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And I mind the time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: -- relating to KLA presence because my learned colleague had asked a few questions. Can you tell me on the 6th of April, was there any fighting between the Serb troops and the KLA in or around Prilepnica?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: On the 13th of April, 1999, was there any fighting in or around Prilepnica between the KLA and the Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: No, sir, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Was any member of the Serbian forces, to your knowledge, wounded on the 6th or on the 13th of April when your village evacuated?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: Yes, a Serb soldier was wounded on the 6th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you know anything --

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: From a ricochet.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know who shot that ricochet?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: I have a map of my village with me. There are two roads there. There's a junction --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry. I'm just asking you for who shot the ricochet, not where it was happening.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: He fired at a metal gate, and then he was wounded himself from a ricochet of the bullet. The bullet ricochetted from the gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And now can you give us the place where the soldier or person fired on the metal gate?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: He was on the road. They were coming from the west towards the centre of the village, and that's where they gathered from all different -- the different directions. And they were firing without control.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Two more questions. Did you leave on the 6th and/or on the 13th of April your village because you were fearful of the KLA engaging in conflict with the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Were you leaving on the 6th or on the 13th of April with all the other villagers of Prilepnica because you were fearful of NATO attacks on your village?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: No, sir, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Has throughout the conflict in 1999 NATO attacked your village?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Why were you leaving on both occasions, on the 6th and the 13th of April, your village? And I'm referring to 1999.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI
utterances.text: On the 6th we were ordered to do so by the military, whereas on the 13th of April we were ordered to do so by the officers that I mentioned. They secured us escort up to Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You will be pleased to know, Mr. Shaqiri, that that completes the questions for you. We've had not only the evidence you've been able to give today but also the earlier statements you've made and the full record of the evidence you gave in the Milutinovic trial. And we'll be absorbing all of that. So we are very grateful that you've been able to come yet again and for the assistance that you've been able to give us. We thank you, and you may of course now return to your normal activities, and the court officer will assist you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, and I wish you success.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I understand that's the evidence available for today, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, we resume on Monday. At this moment I'm not sure whether it's morning or afternoon -- in the afternoon, I'm reminded. I hope we will be able next week and following to have a full body of evidence to use the time that is available to best effort. So we now must adjourn, and we will see you again on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 4th day of May, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 10.37 a.m.,
